results.reasoning: Judged on the scratch copy at :4730 (its own home, identity scratch-judge-0915), by filing notes through both doors the rule names and reading the records back from disk; the rule has no screen. Nearly all of it holds: a known reason is carried as given on CLI and API; bogus, Finding and whitespace-only reasons are refused; a question with a reason is refused on both doors; left unsaid, a person's note files as feedback and an --as-agent / via:agent note as observation; finding and observation are authored agent with no via on disk even when a person typed --reason finding without --as-agent; a decision files as recorded and three attempted transitions out (addressed, open, waived) were refused by CLI and API. The thread-reasons check passes. It fails on one reachable gap: an EMPTY reason. `--reason ""` and `reason: ""` are neither a known word nor unsaid to the code - `reason ?? defaultReason()` keeps the empty string and the vocabulary check is skipped because it is falsy - so the note files with no reason field at all (n-0302 on the copy) and, for a machine, `--as-agent --reason ""` filed n-0310 (API: n-0318) authored under the person with via: agent and no reason; every reader treats a missing reason as feedback, so a machine's note enters the person's queue under the person's name, the exact mark the rule says a finding or observation must not carry. A script passing an unset variable to --reason is a plausible way in. Seen in passing: the CLI refuses with an uncaught stack trace, and its --json echo says by:<person> for a finding whose file says author: agent. Finding filed as n-0295.
